facts.statement: The fossils of Pagosvenator consist of a skull, some vertebrae, and osteoderms that were anonymously donated to the Candelária Museum in 2015.
facts.quote: Despite only being known from a skull and a few vertebrae and osteoderms, which were anonymously donated to the Candelária Museum in 2015

facts.statement: The type species Pagosvenator candelariensis was formally described in 2018.
facts.quote: The type species, Pagosvenator candelariensis, was described in 2018.

facts.statement: Pagosvenator lived during the Mid-Late Triassic in the Dinodontosaurus Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Supergroup in Brazil.
facts.quote: Pagosvenator is an extinct genus of erpetosuchid from the Mid-Late Triassic Dinodontosaurus Assemblage Zone of the Santa Maria Supergroup of Brazil.

facts.statement: Before its formal description in 2018, Pagosvenator was allied with the ornithosuchids.
facts.quote: Pagosvenator is a Brazilian genus which has been allied with the ornithosuchids prior to receiving a formal description in 2018.

facts.statement: Pagosvenator shares traits with other erpetosuchids, including maxillary teeth restricted to the front of the mouth and a maxilla portion under the lacrimal that is higher than long.
facts.quote: It shares a few traits with these other genera, such as maxillary teeth at only the front of the mouth and a portion of the maxilla under the lacrimal which is higher than long.

facts.statement: Pagosvenator lived from the Ladinian to the Carnian stages, between 241.464 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Carnian (241.464 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for Pagosvenator is the family Erpetosuchidae.

rejected.statement: Although the 2018 description compared Pagosvenator only with Erpetosuchus and Parringtonia, its assignment to the erpetosuchid family has some support.
rejected.quote: Although its description only compared it with Erpetosuchus and Parringtonia, its assignment to this family does have some support.
